en: The Questions of King Milinda, Chapter on Time: 8.
The Question on the Reconnection of Name-and-Form
"Venerable Nāgasena, as for that which you call 'name-and-form' (nāmarūpa), therein what is name (nāma) and what is form (rūpa)?
"Whatever is gross therein, O Great King, that is form; whatever subtle mental states and mental factors (cittacetasika-dhammā) are therein, that is name."
“Venerable Nāgasena, for what reason does neither name alone nor form alone undergo rebirth-linking?
“Because these phenomena, O Great King, are mutually dependent; they arise together as one.

“Just as, great king, if there were no embryo in a hen, there would be no egg; and whatever embryo is there and whatever egg is there, both of these are mutually dependent, and their arising is from one and the same source;

even so, great king, if name were not there, form would not be; and whatever name is there and whatever form is there, both of these are mutually dependent, and their arising is from one and the same source.
Thus it has wandered on through this long course.”
This is the eighth dilemma, concerning the linking of name-and-form.
